newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bourse seen continuing its winning ways.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bourse seen continuing its winning ways.

text.p: The Spanish bourse charged to new record highs on Tuesday, and analysts said they expected it to gain further ground by year-end despite temporary declines needed to gather renewed strength.

The IBEX index of 35 leading shares rose to yet another record high at 4,743.43 on Tuesday, having risen 30 percent this year, while the Madrid general index, which has risen 28 percent this year, hit 408.86 at midday.
For the indices 1996 has been a good year, the second best of the last five. Analysts say it has much further to go, with the general index seen possibly exceeding 420 yet this year.
"The market isn't far from profit-taking and we could end the year at levels between today's and the 420 in the Madrid general index," said Juan Cueto, Ibersecurities analyst.
The strong market gains this year have been accompanied by a sharp rise in volumes.
According to official data through October, the value of the number of shares on the Madrid bourse rose to 7.95 trillion pesetas, up 45.7 percent over the same period a year ago.
"In the 410 point zone on the general index we have resistance, but one has to be prepared for a rally in the second half of December," said a dealer at Renta 4 brokerage.
Philippe Sardet, head of Institutional Sales at Credit Lyonnais Securities Espana, was yet more optimistic.
Sardet, who expects a consolidation at around 420 to 425 points, said the general index "could close the year above these levels."
The bourse is benefitting from a favourable economic outlook, including expectations of another Bank of Spain money market rate cut and an improvement in corporate profits.
Expectations that Spain's finances are improving enough to vault it into Europe's single currency project from the start was also underpinning the advance.
"The market has been helped by the improvement in inflation, interest rates and the possibility that Spain might join monetary union from the start," said a dealer.
Experts also pointed to the influx of funds from the debt market, where analysts feel its sharp gains may no longer hold pace with those of stocks, which have lagged behind.
"One key factor is the reallocation of money from debt funds to equities," Cueto said.
They pointed to the boom in new funds indexed to the Ibex-35 and the increasing importance of pension funds to the bourse, which has served to minimize the effect of corrections.
Next year the market is seen making further gains, although these will likely be more moderate than this year.
"A year from now, without being over-optimistic, we could see a rise of 10 to 15 percent in the index," Cueto said.
